task_specification.objective: Repair the two host-gated release-convergence surfaces in this loop: make the dense profile qualify on the supported renderer path, restore a readable traversable cemetery composition with aligned collision and stable landmark visibility, and ensure the upgrade-choice presentation has the required authored visual hierarchy and focus behavior.

diagnosis.root_cause: Release-convergence failures cluster into two different causes: dense-run rendering exceeds the software-renderer frame budget, while the authored cemetery composition has a spatial-integrity defect where the central landmark and traversal framing are not reliably visible/collidable.

stop_conditions: Do not expand scope to deferred menu, ordinary-wave-route, MCP-rebind, or camera-only issues.
Stop dense tuning when the supported renderer meets the frozen frame-time budget or when evidence shows the failure is environment-only and requires host intervention.
Stop spatial edits once the authored map provides readable central/perimeter landmarks, aligned collision, and no disappearance/occlusion during ordinary movement replay.

strategy.rationale: Use a materially different strategy from prior transform-tuning and evidence-only treatments: isolate dense rendering cost behind deterministic quality settings, repair the real upgrade-draft presentation surface, and rebase spatial anchors/collision/camera framing onto the intact authored cemetery package.

code: Run focused static/script checks for the dense-profile quality wrapper, upgrade-draft bindings, and authored-map anchor/collision contract.
Verify native Godot project integrity and host boot remain passing.
runtime: Tester/host recaptures the dense profile with renderer/profile identity and frame-time measurements, then reruns the upgrade draft for rendered hierarchy, focus traversal, truthful values, and selected-build state.
Tester performs direct black-box plus white-box retests for both assigned issue ids and records closure evidence; unsupported renderer behavior is kept as an environment qualification note.
Tester replays movement at spawn, central landmark, bell near-contact, cardinal route, and perimeter checkpoints with before/contact/departure positions and blocked-motion receipts.
visual: Capture sparse shipped-gameplay views for spawn, central building/landmark, cracked bell/keeper-post, perimeter/external depth, and the upgrade-choice page; compare same framing after edits and reject disappearance, occlusion drift, proxy-floor dominance, pass-through, clipped text, or missing focus states.

done_when: A bounded dense-profile run on the supported renderer records frame times within the release budget without runtime errors or visible loss of required gameplay readability.

The implementation exposes a deterministic low-cost dense-profile path that preserves ordinary survivor combat readability; unsupported software-renderer results are clearly surfaced as qualification-only evidence.

The upgrade-choice page leads each option with a recognizable silhouette/icon, shows truthful current-to-new values for no more than three decision-relevant deltas, omits unchanged or placeholder rows, and provides distinct keyboard, mouse, and gamepad focus states without clipping or overlap.
Tester can directly rerun the dense profile and inspect source/settings plus the rendered choice page and selected-build state in one loop.
tasks.instructions: Inspect the dense-run performance path and isolate expensive renderer effects through a product-owned quality wrapper/settings path (such as capped VFX/light/shadow density or batched update cadence) selected at runtime for the dense profile, while preserving ordinary survivor combat readability. In the same bounded quality pass, repair the real upgrade-draft scene/controller so choices use authored icons or silhouettes, compact stat icons, truthful current-to-new deltas (maximum three), restrained copy, and complete keyboard/mouse/gamepad focus handling. Do not alter frozen host controls or claim software-renderer qualification when the environment cannot support it. Add only focused instrumentation needed for a direct same-loop retest, with explicit renderer/profile identity and frame-time receipt.
tasks.title: Isolate dense rendering cost and repair upgrade-choice hierarchy

done_when: The authored cemetery provides larger traversable scale (expand the playable footprint without replacing the intact authored package) plus a coherent external world/external depth beyond the play area.

The central building/landmark and cracked bell/keeper-post landmarks remain readable from spawn and cardinal/route views; no landmark disappearance or camera occlusion occurs during ordinary movement replay.
Player, objective, navigation, and boundary/perimeter collision are rebased to the authored streets/terrain; collision alignment prevents pass-through and keeps movement inside the playable boundary.

Tester can white-box inspect authored-map bindings and collision anchors, then black-box replay movement through spawn, central landmark, and perimeter checkpoints with stable visibility and no disappearance.
tasks.instructions: Repair the authored cemetery composition using the intact map as the sole visual environment: expand to a larger traversable scale and restore external world/external depth, rebase player/objective/navigation/collision and the boundary/perimeter onto native authored streets/terrain, and adjust only the camera/anchor wrapper needed to keep the central building/landmark and bell landmarks readable. Validate ordinary movement/movement replay from spawn through cardinal and perimeter checkpoints, checking collision, no pass-through, and no disappearance/occlusion. Do not add replacement facade/road packs or destructive surgery to the authored package.
